basis: Inherited epidermolytic ichthyosis with hyperkeratosis, erythroderma and blistering; dehydration reported in only 1/4 patients.
Pigment abnormality specifically affecting the eyelid, which belongs to the ocular axis.
Inherited platelet dysfunction, thrombocytopenia and beta-thalassemia; splenic involvement is also haematologic. Petechiae do not establish skin disease.
Isolated oocyte maturation failure causing infertility and implantation failure; no endocrine dysfunction or other covered organ disease established.
Progressive neurodegenerative impairment of speech motor planning.
B-lymphoblastic blood/marrow neoplasm; the leukemia/lymphoma entity also qualifies for the lymphoma mechanism axis.
Benign neoplasm arising in mammary ducts; breast has no axis.
Ovotesticular development and ambiguous genitalia concern reproductive anatomy; endocrine dysfunction is not established.
Mitochondrial metabolic defect; cardiomyopathy in 80-99%, neurodevelopmental dysfunction in at least 30%. Hypotonia and enzyme findings alone do not establish common destructive myopathy.
Photosensitive skin disease with scarring; developmental delay and intellectual disability in 1/1 reported patient. Photophobia alone does not establish ocular damage.
Psychotic disorder without a covered organ disease; cognitive symptoms belong to the psychiatric syndrome, and structural brain abnormalities are occasional.
Degenerative, immune-mediated skeletal myopathy. Dysphagia reflects swallowing-muscle involvement rather than an independently damaged gastrointestinal organ.
Developmental delay is common across clinically recognized chromosome 12 deletion syndromes; other organ malformations vary with the deleted segment.
Hepatic fibrosis and regenerative nodules define cirrhosis; encephalopathy, varices and renal syndromes are separately diagnosed complications.
GAG storage with skeletal dysplasia; valvular disease and airway obstruction each affect over 50% over the course. Common hearing loss omitted under the four-axis cap.
Abnormal spacing of the medial eyelid canthi; an ocular adnexal disorder.
Yersinia pestis infection of lymphatic tissue; blood, pulmonary and other organ complications are not defining or uniformly common.
Disordered intestinal stool output; this umbrella includes infectious and noninfectious causes, so infection is not universal.
Skeletal dysplasia, immunodeficiency and neurodevelopmental abnormalities define the syndrome; developmental delay 6/6 and SCID 7/12. Pneumonia is a separate infection.
Isolated underdevelopment of the retinal fovea causing reduced visual acuity; no systemic pathology by definition.
Persistent disease of multiple peripheral nerves; metabolic and immune mechanisms apply only to particular subtypes.
Prenatal alcohol-related neurodevelopmental impairment involving cognition, regulation and adaptive functioning.
Small-bowel villous injury and collagen deposition cause malabsorption. The metabolic parent alone does not establish a primary metabolic defect; immune causation remains uncertain.
Endogenous microbial ethanol production defines a metabolic disorder; fermentation does not establish local tissue damage or infection, and intoxication is transient.
Neonatal surfactant deficiency causes alveolar dysfunction and impaired pulmonary gas exchange.
